Cue Card
Describe a time when you used your imagination. You should say: when it was, what you imagined, what you did with the idea, and explain how it made you feel.
描述一次你运用想象力的经历。你应该说：什么时候 / 你想象了什么 / 你用这个想法做了什么 / 并解释你的感受
Answer
When I was about ten years old, I had this wild idea that I wanted to invent a platform where people could build their own worlds. It was not a game exactly, it was more like a digital space with various functions—places for thematic activities and personal spaces where everyone could create and record their own experiences. I imagined it would have different themed sections where people could design environments, organize collaborative projects, and keep a personal record of what they built. I remember spending hours filling notebooks with these designs, completely lost in the process. Of course, at that age I had no idea how to code or build software, so the project never became real in a technical sense. But the act of imagining itself was profoundly meaningful to me. It gave me a sense of agency and possibility that shaped how I think about creativity even today. Looking back, I realize that my later choice to study directing and now education both stem from that early impulse to create spaces where people can express themselves and construct their own meaning.
大约十岁的时候，我有一个疯狂的想法，想发明一个让人们可以构建自己世界的平台。它不完全是游戏，更像是一个数字空间，任何人都可以设计环境、创造角色，并和他人分享自己想象中的宇宙。我甚至画了界面草图，有地形、天气和生物等不同模块。我记得花了好几个小时在笔记本上画这些设计，完全沉浸其中。当然，在那个年龄我完全不知道怎么编程或开发软件，所以这个项目在技术意义上从未实现。但想象的行为本身对我意义深远。它给了我一种主动性和可能性，至今仍影响着我对创造力的看法。回头看，我后来选择学编导、现在转向教育，都源于那种早期想要创造让人表达自我、构建意义的空间的冲动。
Part 3
Do you think schools should encourage imagination more?
Absolutely. In many education systems, including China's, there is a heavy emphasis on standardized testing and correct answers, which can squeeze out imaginative thinking. Schools should create space for open-ended projects where there is no single right answer, because that is closer to how real-world problems actually work.
绝对应该。在包括中国在内的许多教育体系中，标准化考试和正确答案被过分强调，这可能挤压想象力的空间。学校应该为开放式项目创造空间，因为那更接近真实世界问题的运作方式。
Part 3
Can imagination be taught, or is it innate?
I believe everyone is born with imaginative capacity, but it can be nurtured or suppressed depending on the environment. It is less about teaching imagination from scratch and more about removing the barriers that block it, things like fear of being wrong or too much structure.
我相信每个人天生都有想象的能力，但环境可以培养它也可以压制它。与其说是从零教起，不如说是移除阻碍想象力的障碍，比如害怕犯错或过度结构化。
Part 2&3重要决定
▶
Cue Card
Describe an important decision you made. You should say: what the decision was, when you made it, why you made it, and explain how it affected your life.
描述一个你做出的重要决定。你应该说：决定是什么 / 什么时候做的 / 为什么做这个决定 / 并解释它如何影响了你的生活
Answer
The most important decision I have made so far was choosing to pursue a master's degree in education in the UK rather than continuing on the directing and media career path I had been trained for. I made this decision during my final year of university, after a period of careful thought about what I actually wanted from my career. I realized that while I loved the craft of filmmaking, I was more drawn to the way storytelling can teach people, how media could be used to teach, to inspire, and to create understanding between people. The decision was not easy. My family had expected me to work in television or film production, and switching to education felt like starting from scratch. But my cousin's story of leaving banking to study law gave me the courage to trust my own instincts. I spent months researching programs, preparing for IELTS with my Filipino tutor, and writing applications. This decision has basically reshaped my trajectory. It has pushed me out of my comfort zone, improved my English dramatically, and given me a clearer sense of purpose than I have ever had before.
到目前为止我做的最重要的决定，是选择去英国读教育学硕士，而不是继续走我一直受训的编导和媒体职业道路。这个决定是在大学最后一年做的，经过了一段关于我真正想从职业中获得什么的深度反思。我意识到虽然我热爱电影制作的技艺，但我更被叙事的教育维度所吸引，媒体如何用来教学、激发灵感、在人与人之间创造理解。这个决定并不容易。家人原本期望我在电视或电影行业工作，转向教育感觉像是从零开始。但堂哥离开银行去学法律的故事给了我勇气去相信自己的直觉。我花了几个月研究项目、和外教一起准备雅思、写申请。这个决定从根本上重塑了我的轨迹。它把我推出了舒适区，大幅提升了我的英语水平，也给了我一前所未有的目标感。
Part 3
What factors should people consider when making important decisions?
I think people should consider both practical and emotional factors. Practically, you need to assess finances, timeline, and feasibility. Emotionally, you need to ask whether the decision aligns with your core values and whether you can live with the regret of not trying.
我认为人们应该同时考虑实际和情感因素。实际层面，你需要评估财务、时间线和可行性。情感层面，你需要问这个决定是否符合你的核心价值观，以及你是否能承受不尝试的遗憾。
Part 3
Do you think it is harder to make decisions now than in the past?
In some ways yes, because we have too many options. In the past, career paths were more linear — you studied one thing and did it for life. Now, the possibilities are endless, which is liberating but also paralyzing. Social media makes it worse by showing us all the paths we didn't take. I think feeling tired from making too many choices is a real modern phenomenon.
在某种程度上是的，因为我们有太多选择。过去职业路径更加线性——你学一样东西就做一辈子。现在可能性是无限的，这既解放也令人瘫痪。社交媒体让情况更糟，因为它向我们展示了所有没有选择的路。我认为决策疲劳是真实的现代现象。
Part 3
Do you think young people today make decisions more independently?
In some ways yes, because access to information allows young people to research options thoroughly before consulting anyone. But I also think the abundance of choices can actually make decision-making harder, leading to analysis paralysis where people delay choosing altogether.
在某些方面是的，因为获取信息的便利让年轻人在咨询任何人之前就能充分研究选项。但我也认为选择的丰富反而可能让决策变得更难，导致分析瘫痪，人们干脆拖延不做选择。
Part 2&3近期改变的计划
▶
Cue Card
Describe a plan you changed recently. You should say: what the original plan was, why you changed it, what the new plan is, and explain how you feel about the change.
描述一个你最近改变了的计划。你应该说：原来的计划是什么 / 为什么改变 / 新计划是什么 / 并解释你对改变的感受
Answer
Recently I changed my study plan for the IELTS exam. Originally, I had intended to take the test in March, which would have given me a comfortable buffer before my UK program started. However, as I progressed through my preparation, I realized that my speaking score was still falling short of the 6.5 target. My Filipino tutor honestly told me that my pronunciation and fluency needed more work than I had anticipated. At first, I felt frustrated and tempted to just push through with the original timeline. But after talking it over with my childhood friend, who reminded me that rushing rarely produces good results, I decided to postpone the exam by two months. The new plan involved increasing my speaking practice sessions from twice a week to four times a week, and focusing specifically on Part 2 monologues where I tended to lose coherence. Looking back, this was absolutely the right call. My speaking improved noticeably, and I felt far more confident walking into the exam room. The experience taught me that being willing to adjust your plans is not a failure, but a mature choice.
最近我改变了雅思考试的备考计划。原计划是三月份考试，这样在英国项目开学前有充裕的缓冲时间。但随着备考推进，我发现口语分数仍达不到6.5的目标。菲律宾外教坦率地告诉我，我的发音和流利度需要比预期更多的练习。起初我很沮丧，很想按原计划硬冲。但和发小谈了之后，他提醒我仓促很少有好结果，我决定把考试推迟两个月。新计划包括把口语练习从每周两次增加到四次，并专门针对我容易失去连贯性的Part 2独白部分进行训练。回头看，这绝对是对的决定。我的口语明显进步了，走进考场时也自信了很多。这次经历让我明白，愿意调整计划不是失败的标志，而是成熟的标志。
Part 3
Why do people sometimes need to change their plans?
Plans are based on assumptions about the future, and when reality does not match those assumptions, adjustment becomes necessary. Sometimes new information emerges, sometimes circumstances beyond our control intervene, and sometimes we simply underestimate how long something will take.
计划是基于对未来的假设，当现实与这些假设不符时，调整就变得必要。有时新信息出现，有时超出我们控制的情况发生，有时我们只是低估了某件事需要的时间。
Part 3
How can people better handle unexpected changes to their plans?
By building flexibility into their mindset from the start. If you view plans as intentions rather than contracts, changes feel less like failures. Also, having a Plan B ready reduces panic. The most adaptable people I know expect disruption and see it as an opportunity rather than a catastrophe.
通过从一开始就在心态中建立灵活性。如果你将计划视为意图而非合同，变化就不太像失败。另外，准备好B计划减少恐慌。我认识的最适应力强的人预料到干扰，并将其视为机会而非灾难。
Part 2&3想从事医疗行业的人
▶
Cue Card
Describe a person you know who wants to work in the medical field. You should say: who this person is, what they want to do, why they chose this field, and explain how you feel about their choice.
描述一个你认识的想在医疗领域工作的人。你应该说：这个人是谁 / 他想做什么 / 为什么选择这个领域 / 并解释你对他选择的感受
Answer
The person I want to talk about is a close friend from university who is now studying to become a pediatrician. We met during our first year at Sichuan University of Media and Communications, where she was actually studying communications before deciding to switch tracks entirely. Her decision was deeply personal. When she was in high school, her younger brother was diagnosed with a serious illness, and she spent months in and out of hospitals. The experience was terrifying, but she was struck by how much difference a caring and competent doctor could make in a family's darkest moments. She told me that she wanted to be that person for other families. After completing her communications degree, she began taking prerequisite science courses and is now preparing for medical school entrance exams. What strikes me most about her is the quiet determination she brings to this path. She knows it will take many more years of study and that the workload will be very large, but she never wavers. I feel a deep respect for her choice, and in a way, her courage mirrors what my cousin did in switching from banking to law. Both of them chose meaning over convenience.
我想说的是大学时一个好朋友，她现在正在为成为儿科医生而学习。我们在四川传媒学院第一年认识，她当时其实学的是传播学，后来决定完全转换方向。她的决定非常私人。高中时她弟弟被诊断出重病，她来来回回在医院待了好几个月。那段经历很可怕，但她被一个有爱心和能力的医生在一个家庭最黑暗时刻所能带来的改变深深触动。她告诉我她想成为其他家庭的那个人。完成传播学学位后，她开始修 prerequisite 科学课程，现在正在准备医学院入学考试。最让我印象深刻的是她在这条路上展现的安静决心。她知道还需要很多年的学习，工作量会很大，但她从不动摇。我对她的选择深怀敬意，某种程度上，她的勇气和我堂哥从银行转学法律如出一辙。他们都选择了意义而非便利。
Part 3
Why do some people choose difficult careers like medicine?
I think it comes down to a combination of calling and capability. Some people feel a real vocation to help others, and medicine offers the most direct way to do that. Others are drawn by the intellectual challenge, the human body is endlessly complex, and some personalities thrive on that kind of problem-solving.
我认为这归结于使命感和能力的结合。有些人真正感受到帮助他人的使命感，而医学提供了最直接的途径。另一些人被智力挑战所吸引，人体无比复杂，某些性格的人正是在那种问题解决中如鱼得水。
Part 3
Do you think medical professionals are valued enough in society?
This is a complex issue. During health crises, medical professionals are rightly celebrated as heroes, but in ordinary times their working conditions and compensation do not always reflect their importance. There is often a gap between societal appreciation and practical support.
这是个复杂的问题。在健康危机期间，医疗专业人员理所当然地被誉为英雄，但在平时他们的工作条件和薪酬并不总能反映他们的重要性。社会赞誉和实际支持之间常常存在差距。
Part 2&3早起经历
▶
Cue Card
Describe a time when you got up early. You should say: when it was, why you got up early, what you did, and explain how you felt about it.
描述一次你早起的日子。你应该说：什么时候 / 为什么早起 / 你做了什么 / 并解释你的感受
Answer
A memorable early morning was when I got up at five o'clock to catch the sunrise from a mountain near my hometown in Shanxi. I had been feeling mentally drained from weeks of IELTS preparation, and my childhood friend suggested that a hike might clear my head. We left while it was still dark, walking through empty village paths that felt almost surreal without the usual daytime sounds. The hike itself was challenging, the dirt trail was steep and the air was cold, but reaching the summit just as the first light broke over the hills was absolutely worth it. The sky shifted from deep blue to gold, and the whole valley below slowly emerged from the mist. I remember standing there feeling a profound sense of stillness that I had not experienced in months. That morning reminded me that sometimes one of the best things you can do is step away from your desk and let nature reset your view. I came back to my studies with renewed energy and a clearer mind.
一个难忘的清晨是我五点起床去老家附近的山上看日出。连续几周的雅思备考让我精神上很疲惫，发小建议去爬山清清脑子。我们在天还没亮时离开城市，穿过空无一人的街道，没有平时的车流，感觉几乎超现实。爬山本身很有挑战性，石阶陡峭，空气寒冷，但在第一缕阳光洒过山顶时到达山顶绝对值得。天空从深蓝变成金色，下面的整个山谷慢慢从雾中浮现。我记得站在那里感受到一种几个月来没有体验过的深深的宁静。那个早晨提醒我，有时候你能做的最高效的事就是离开书桌，让自然重置你的视角。我带着新的能量和更清晰的头脑回到了学习中。
Part 3
Do you think it is better to get up early or stay up late?
I think it depends on your biological rhythm. Some people are naturally more productive in the morning, while others do their best thinking at night. the key is to be consistent, forcing yourself into a schedule that fights your natural clock usually backfires.
我觉得取决于你的生物节律。有些人天生早上效率更高，另一些人晚上思维最活跃。关键是规律，强迫自己进入一个和自然生物钟对抗的日程通常会适得其反。
Part 3
Why do some people find it hard to get up early?
Modern lifestyles are a big factor. Late-night screen time disrupts sleep quality, and irregular schedules confuse the body's internal clock. Also, if there is no compelling reason to get up early, the motivation simply is not there.
现代生活方式是一个大因素。睡前看屏幕会影响睡眠质量，不规律的作息会打乱身体的生物钟。另外，如果没有一个足够 interesting 的早起理由，动力根本就不存在。
Part 2&3机智解决问题的人
▶
Cue Card
Describe a person who solved a problem in a clever way. You should say: who the person was, what the problem was, how they solved it, and explain why you think it was clever.
描述一个用聪明方式解决问题的人。你应该说：这个人是谁 / 问题是什么 / 他怎么解决的 / 并解释为什么你觉得很聪明
Answer
I want to talk about my childhood friend, who once solved a problem during our university graduation film project that I still think was surprisingly clever. We were shooting a documentary about street food vendors in Chengdu, and we had secured permission to film at a popular night market. But on the day of the shoot, it started raining heavily, and most of the vendors had put away their stalls. We were panicking because we had a deadline and no backup plan. My friend, without hesitation, went over to the few vendors who had stayed open under makeshift shelters and started helping them serve customers. He chatted with them, learned their stories, and slowly built enough rapport that they agreed to let us film even in the rain. He then suggested we reframe the documentary to focus on how these vendors persevere through bad weather, which turned out to be a much more interesting angle than our original concept. The problem was not just solved, it was changed into an opportunity. That is what made his way so clever, he did not force the original plan but adapted to reality and found a better story in the process.
我想说的是我的发小，他在我们大学毕业电影项目中解决了一个问题，我至今觉得非常巧妙。我们在拍一部关于成都街头摊贩的纪录片，已经获得了在一个热门夜市的拍摄许可。但开拍当天突然下大雨，大部分摊贩都收摊了。我们很慌，因为deadline在即又没有备用方案。我的朋友毫不犹豫地走到少数几个在临时遮棚下还在营业的摊贩那里，开始帮他们招待客人。他跟他们聊天，了解他们的故事，逐渐建立了足够的信任，他们同意让我们在雨中拍摄。然后他建议我们把纪录片重新定位，聚焦这些摊贩如何在恶劣天气中坚持营业，结果这个角度比我们原来的概念更有吸引力。问题不仅被解决了，还被转化成了一个机会。这就是他的方法之所以巧妙的原因，他没有强行执行原计划，而是适应现实并在过程中找到了更好的故事。
Part 3
What kinds of problems require creative solutions?
Problems that are unpredictable and context-dependent usually require creative thinking. When there is no established playbook, like dealing with a sudden change during a film shoot or navigating a cultural misunderstanding, you have to improvise based on the specific situation rather than following a formula.
那些不可预测且依赖具体情境的问题通常需要创造性思维。当没有现成的方法可循时，比如拍摄中突然变化或处理文化误解，你必须根据具体情况即兴发挥而不是照公式来。
Part 3
Can creative problem-solving be taught?
I believe it can be nurtured through exposure to diverse situations and by encouraging people to reframe problems rather than just solving them. Case studies, role plays, and real-world projects are all effective ways to develop this kind of flexible thinking.
我相信它可以通过接触多样化情境以及鼓励人们重新定义问题而非仅仅是解决问题来培养。案例研究、角色扮演和真实项目都是培养这种灵活思维的有效方式。
Part 2&3别人帮助解决问题
▶
Cue Card
Describe a time when someone helped you solve a problem. You should say: who helped you, what the problem was, how they helped you, and explain how you felt about it.
描述一次别人帮你解决问题的经历。你应该说：谁帮了你 / 问题是什么 / 他怎么帮的 / 并解释你的感受
Answer
I want to talk about a time when my Filipino English tutor helped me overcome a major obstacle in my IELTS preparation. The problem was with my writing task, specifically the argumentative essay. I kept scoring around 5.5 and could not figure out why my essays were not improving despite weeks of practice. My tutor sat down with me and went through several of my essays line by line. He identified a structural issue that I had been completely blind to: my paragraphs were technically correct but lacked logical progression. Each paragraph made a point, but the points did not build on each other to form a coherent argument. He then taught me a simple framework for connecting ideas, using transition phrases that showed cause and effect rather than just listing points. He also showed me how to write a thesis statement that actually guided the entire essay. Within three weeks of applying his advice, my writing score moved up to 6.5. I felt immensely grateful, not just for the technical help but for the patience and honesty he showed in telling me what I was doing wrong.
我想说的是菲律宾英语外教帮我克服了雅思备考中一个重大障碍的经历。问题出在写作部分，具体说是议论文。我的分数一直停在5.5左右，搞不清为什么练习了好几周还是没有提升。外教和我坐下来逐行分析了好几篇我的作文。他发现了一个我完全没有意识到的结构性问题：我的段落从技术上说没问题，但缺乏逻辑递进。每段都提出了观点，但观点之间没有相互构建形成一个连贯的论证。然后他教了我一个连接想法的简单框架，使用表示因果的过渡短语而不是简单地列举观点。他还教我怎么写一个能真正指导整篇文章的中心论点句。用了他的建议后三周内，我的写作分数就提升到了6.5。我感到无比感激，不仅是技术上的帮助，更是他在告诉我哪里做错了时展现的耐心和诚实。
Part 3
Do you think it is better to solve problems alone or ask for help?
I think it depends on the nature of the problem. For problems that require personal reflection or creative insight, working alone can be more productive. But when you are stuck in a blind spot, as I was with my writing, an outside view is invaluable and can save you very large amounts of time.
我觉得取决于问题的性质。对于需要个人反思或创造性洞察的问题，独自工作可能更有效。但当你陷入盲点时，就像我写作那样，外部视角是无价的，可以为你节省大量时间。
Part 3
What skills are needed to help others solve problems?
First, active listening — you need to understand the problem fully before offering solutions. Second, analytical thinking — the ability to break down someone else's situation and identify what they're missing. And third, empathy — because people who are stuck often feel frustrated or embarrassed, so how you deliver help matters as much as the help itself. My tutor didn't just correct my essays; he made me feel like the problem was solvable.
首先，积极倾听——你需要在给出解决方案之前完全理解问题。其次，分析思维——能够拆解别人的处境并找出他们遗漏的。第三，同理心——因为陷入困境的人往往感到沮丧或尴尬，所以你提供帮助的方式和帮助本身一样重要。我的外教不只是纠正了我的作文，他让我觉得问题是可解决的。
Part 2&3想颁布的新法律
▶
Cue Card
Describe a new law you would like to see introduced. You should say: what the law would be, who it would affect, how it would work, and explain why you think it is necessary.
描述一项你想看到实施的新法律。你应该说：法律会是什么 / 会影响谁 / 如何运作 / 并解释为什么你觉得有必要
Answer
If I could introduce a new law, it would be a comprehensive digital privacy protection law specifically focused on educational data. As someone about to study education, I have been researching how student data is collected, stored, and sometimes exploited by educational technology companies. The law I envision would require all ed-tech platforms to obtain explicit parental consent before collecting any data from minors under sixteen. It would also mandate that student data cannot be sold to or shared with third-party advertisers under any circumstances. Furthermore, companies would be required to delete all student data upon graduation or upon the student's request. The reason I think this law is necessary is that children are generating very large amounts of digital data through online learning platforms, often without anyone realizing the long-term implications. This data can include learning patterns, behavioral tendencies, and even emotional states. My cousin, who works in law, once told me that the legal framework around digital privacy in China is still developing, and I believe education is the area most urgently in need of targeted regulation. Children should be able to learn online without their data becoming a commodity.
如果我能制定一部新法律，那将是一部专门针对教育数据的全面数字隐私保护法。作为一个即将学习教育学的人，我一直在研究学生数据是如何被教育科技公司收集、存储甚至利用的。我设想的法律将要求所有教育科技平台在收集十六岁以下未成年人的任何数据之前必须获得明确的家长同意。它还规定学生数据在任何情况下都不得出售或分享给第三方广告商。此外，公司在学生毕业或学生要求时必须删除所有学生数据。我认为这部法律之所以必要，是因为孩子们通过在线学习平台产生了大量数字数据，而往往没有人意识到其长期影响。这些数据可以包括学习模式、行为倾向甚至情绪状态。我从事法律工作的堂哥曾告诉我，中国数字隐私的法律框架仍在发展中，我认为教育是最迫切需要针对性监管的领域。孩子们应该能够在网上学习，而不用让自己的数据变成商品。
Part 3
Do you think laws can keep up with technological change?
This is one of the fundamental challenges of modern governance. Technology evolves at a pace that outstrips the process of making laws, which is deliberately slow and deliberative. I think the solution is not faster laws but more principles-based regulation that can adapt to new technologies without needing to be rewritten constantly.
这是现代治理面临的基本挑战之一。技术发展的速度超越了立法过程，而后者刻意是缓慢和审慎的。我认为解决方案不是更快的法律，而是更多基于原则的监管，能够适应新技术而不需要不断重写。
Part 3
Should young people have a say in making laws that affect them?
Absolutely. Laws affecting digital natives should not be written exclusively by people who did not grow up with the internet. Young people bring a lived understanding of how technology actually works in daily life, which is something that theory alone cannot replace.
当然。影响数字原住民的法律不应该完全由没有在互联网时代长大的人来制定。年轻人带来了对技术如何在日常生活中实际运作的切身理解，这是纯理论知识无法替代的。
Part 2&3想从事的短期海外工作
▶
Cue Card
Describe a short-term job abroad you would like to do. You should say: what the job would be, where you would do it, how long it would last, and explain why you would like to do it.
描述一份你想做的海外短期工作。你应该说：工作是什么 / 在哪里做 / 持续多久 / 并解释为什么你想做
Answer
The short-term job I would love to do is working as a media workshop instructor at a community education center in the UK, ideally for about three to six months during or after my master's program. The job would involve teaching basic filmmaking and digital storytelling skills to teenagers from underprivileged backgrounds, helping them use video as a tool for self-expression and community involvement. I would want to do this in a city like Manchester or Birmingham, where there are lively community arts programs but also real socioeconomic disparities that limit access to creative education. The reason this appeals to me so strongly is that it sits at the exact intersection of my two passions, directing and education. I have always believed that storytelling is not just an art form but a way for people to make sense of their lives and assert their voices. Working with young people who might not otherwise have access to media training would be incredibly fulfilling. It would also give me practical experience in educational media, which is the field I hope to build a career in after graduation.
我想做的短期工作是在英国一个社区教育中心担任媒体工作坊讲师，最好在硕士项目期间或之后做三到六个月。工作内容是教来自弱势背景的青少年基础电影制作和数字叙事技能，帮助他们用视频作为自我表达和社区参与的工具。我想在曼彻斯特或伯明翰这样的城市做，那里有活跃的社区艺术项目，但也存在真实的社含经济差距，限制了创意教育的获取。这个工作之所以如此吸引我，是因为它恰好位于我两个热情的交汇点：编导和教育。我一直相信讲故事不仅仅是艺术形式，更是人们理解自己生活、发出自己声音的方式。和那些可能没有机会接受媒体培训的年轻人一起工作会非常有成就感。它还能给我教育媒体方面的实践经验，这是我毕业后希望建立事业的领域。
Part 3
What are the benefits of working abroad?
Working abroad forces you to adapt to a different culture and work environment, which builds strength after setbacks and the ability to work with people from other cultures. It also broadens your professional network across borders, which is increasingly valuable in a globalized economy. The main challenge, of course, is being away from your support system.
在国外工作迫使你适应不同的文化和工作环境，这培养了韧性和跨文化能力。它还让你跨越国界拓展职业人脉，这在全球化经济中越来越有价值。当然主要挑战是远离你的支持系统。
Part 3
Do you think short-term international experiences are valuable for young people?
Yes, I think they are incredibly valuable because they offer a short period of cultural immersion without the long-term commitment of relocation. Short-term experiences are often more accessible and can serve as a stepping stone that helps young people decide whether they want to pursue longer international opportunities.
是的，我认为它们非常有价值，因为它们提供了一种浓缩的文化沉浸体验，而不需要长期迁移的承诺。短期经历通常更容易获得，可以作为一块跳板，帮助年轻人决定是否要追求更长期的国际机会。
Part 2&3喜欢画画的孩子
▶
Cue Card
Describe a child you know who likes drawing or painting. You should say: who the child is, what they like to draw, how they developed this interest, and explain why you think they enjoy it.
描述一个你认识的喜欢画画的孩子。你应该说：这个孩子是谁 / 喜欢画什么 / 怎么发展出这个兴趣的 / 并解释为什么你觉得他喜欢画画
Answer
I'd like to talk about myself as a child, because drawing was an absolute obsession of mine throughout my early years. From around age six to twelve, I would spend hours every evening with my colored pencils and sketchbooks, completely absorbed in creating my own visual worlds. What I loved most was drawing elaborate city skylines. Growing up in Shanxi, I was fascinated by the rapid urban change happening around me — cranes on the horizon, new towers rising seemingly overnight. I would sketch these emerging skylines from memory, then embellish them with imagined structures: floating gardens between buildings, bridges connecting rooftops, spiral towers that defied gravity. My interest was nurtured by my parents, who never dismissed my drawings as childish scribbles. My father would sometimes sit beside me and ask me to narrate the stories behind each building, which made me feel that my imagination was worth sharing. Looking back, I realize this early passion for visual storytelling directly led me to study film and television directing, and ultimately toward my current aspiration in education — because I believe creativity flourishes when children are given space and encouragement rather than rigid instructions.
我想谈谈小时候的自己，因为画画在我整个童年时期是一种绝对的痴迷。大约从六岁到十二岁，我每天晚上都会花好几个小时拿着彩色铅笔和速写本，完全沉浸在创造自己视觉世界中。我最喜欢画的是精心绘制的城市天际线。在山西长大，我被身边快速的城市变化所吸引——天际线上的塔吊、仿佛一夜之间拔地而起的新楼。我会凭记忆画出这些正在成形的天际线，然后加上想象的建筑：楼与楼之间的空中花园、连接屋顶的天桥、违反重力的螺旋塔。我的兴趣得到了父母的培养，他们从不把我的画当作小孩子的涂鸦而轻视。我父亲有时会坐在我旁边，让我讲述每栋建筑背后的故事，这让我觉得自己的想象力是值得分享的。回想起来，我意识到这种早期对视觉叙事的热情直接引导我学习了影视编导专业，并最终走向了我目前的教育志向——因为我相信，当孩子被给予空间和鼓励而非刻板指令时，创造力才能真正绽放。
Part 3
Do you think art education is important for children's development?
I consider it essential, though it is often undervalued in systems that put first test scores. Art education develops capacities that other subjects cannot easily replicate — the ability to understand space and shapes, emotional expression, and the ability to tolerate ambiguity and explore multiple solutions to a single problem. When children draw or paint, they are not just making pictures; they are learning to observe the world closely and translate their perceptions into something communicable, which is a basic cognitive and life skill.
我认为它至关重要，尽管在以考试分数为优先的体系中它常被低估。艺术教育培养的是其他学科难以替代的能力——空间推理、情感表达，以及对模糊性的容忍和探索单一问题多种解决方案的能力。当孩子画画时，他们不仅仅是在制作图像；他们是在学习仔细观察世界，并将自己的感知转化为可传达的东西，这是一种基本的认知能力和生活技能。
Part 3
Should children be encouraged to pursue art as a career?
I think they should be encouraged to explore art without pressure, but whether it becomes a career should be their own decision. The reality is that art careers are financially uncertain, and parents' concerns are valid. However, discouraging children entirely from art can stifle a skill that's valuable in many fields — design, communication, problem-solving. The best way is to let art enrich their development while helping them understand the real situation.
我认为应该鼓励他们无压力地探索艺术，但是否以此为职业应该是他们自己的决定。现实是艺术职业在经济上不确定，家长的担忧是合理的。但完全阻止孩子接触艺术可能会压制一项在许多领域都有价值的技能——设计、沟通、解决问题。最好的方法是让艺术丰富他们的发展，同时帮助他们了解现实情况。
Part 2&3完美工作
▶
Cue Card
Describe what you think would be the perfect job for you. You should say: what the job would be, what skills it requires, why you think it would be perfect, and explain how you plan to achieve it.
描述你心目中完美的工作。你应该说：工作是什么 / 需要什么技能 / 为什么觉得它完美 / 并解释你计划如何实现
Answer
The perfect job for me would be an educational content creator — someone who designs innovative learning materials that combine visual storytelling with how well it helps people learn. Essentially, I envision bridging the gap between media production and education, using the directing skills I developed during my undergraduate studies to make learning more interesting and accessible. This role would require a diverse skill set: a solid understanding of educational theory, proficiency in video production and visual design, and the ability to translate complex concepts into interesting stories. It would also demand empathy — the ability to understand where learners struggle and to anticipate what might spark their curiosity. What makes this job perfect for me is that it aligns with both my background and my aspirations. My undergraduate degree in film and television directing gave me the tools to craft stories visually, and my upcoming Master's in Education in the UK will equip me with the basic knowledge I need. I see these two paths not as separate but as complementary threads of the same tapestry. Ultimately, I want to create content that democratizes access to quality education, particularly for students in regions where traditional resources are limited. That, to me, would be work worth waking up for every day.
我心目中的完美工作是教育内容创作者——设计创新学习材料，将视觉叙事与教学效果结合起来的人。本质上，我希望弥合媒体制作与教育之间的鸿沟，利用本科期间学到的编导技能让学习变得更吸引人、更易获得。这个角色需要多元化的技能组合：扎实的教育理论知识、视频制作与视觉设计的专业能力，以及将复杂概念转化为引人入胜叙事的能力。它还需要同理心——理解学习者的困难所在，预判什么能激发他们的好奇心。这份工作之所以完美，是因为它同时契合我的背景和志向。我的影视编导本科学位赋予了我视觉叙事的工具，而即将在英国攻读的教育学硕士将为我提供所需的理论基础。我认为这两条路径不是分离的，而是同一幅织锦中互补的两根线。最终，我希望创作的内容能让优质教育触手可及，特别是为那些传统资源有限地区的学生。对我来说，这才是值得每天早起的工作。
Part 3
What qualities do you think are most important for a fulfilling career?
In my view, the most essential quality is a real sense of purpose — the feeling that your work helps something beyond yourself. Beyond that, I'd say continuous growth and creative autonomy are important. A fulfilling career should challenge you to keep learning while giving you enough freedom to experiment and bring your own view. When these elements align with your natural interests and strengths, work stops feeling like obligation and becomes a form of self-expression, which I think is a very strong form of job satisfaction one can achieve.
在我看来，最重要的品质是一种真正的使命感——觉得自己的工作在为超越自身的事情做贡献。除此之外，我认为持续成长和创作自主权也至关重要。一份令人满足的职业应该在不断挑战你学习的同时，给予你足够的自由去尝试、去注入自己的视角。当这些要素与你的天赋兴趣和优势对齐时，工作就不再感觉像义务，而变成了一种自我表达的形式——我认为这是人所能达到的最高层次的职业满足感。
Part 3
Do you think job satisfaction is more important than salary?
For me, yes — but I recognize this is a privilege that not everyone can afford. When basic needs aren't met, salary understandably comes first. But once you reach a reasonable standard of living, research shows that additional income has diminishing returns on happiness, while purpose and growth continue to matter more. The ideal scenario is finding a job that pays enough to feel secure and gives you a sense of meaningful contribution.
对我来说是的——但我认识到这是一种并非所有人都能负担的特权。当基本需求未满足时，薪水优先是完全可以理解的。但一旦达到合理的生活水平，研究表明额外收入对幸福感的回报递减，而使命感和成长则持续更重要。理想的场景是找到一份既能给你安全感、又能让你感到有意义的贡献的工作。

6.5分技巧

📝阅读建议：5分钟浏览，理解差异即可。考前可快速复习对照表。

从 6 分到 6.5 分的词汇升级对照、关键提升动作、详细对比案例与提升路径。

6 分和 7 分的核心差异不在"词汇难度"，而在精确度、句型多样性和因果链完整度。 以下对比基于 331 组 6/7 分范文的文本统计。
五大提升维度
维度6分特征7分特征提升策略
词汇精确度 good / bad / interesting / very / really impressive / negative / fascinating / truly / really 用更精确的同义词替换泛用词，但不必追求"大词"
句型多样性 I like... because... and... so... which 从句 / Although 让步 / Not only...but also / 分词结构 每个回答至少使用 2 种不同句型结构
因果链完整度 给出原因但不展开后果 原因→条件→结果→影响 完整链条 在 because 后加 If...then 或 which means... 补充后果
连接词分层 also / and / but / so On top of that / While / That said / Since 按逻辑层选词：立场→因果→举例→让步→递进
细节具体化 "I visit galleries" "I often visit local galleries—it's become my go-to activity for unwinding" 加入频率、地点、感受、比喻等细节

词汇升级对照表（8组核心对照）

6分表达6.5分表达
I like artI'm really into art
It was funIt was incredibly fulfilling
I was surprisedWhat surprised me was...
It's importantIt carries the weight of...
I learned thatIt taught me that...
The cake was niceWhat made it special was the story behind it
I go walkingI follow the green lights
I think it's goodI personally care deeply about

词汇升级对照表

6分表达7分升级主题说明
really enjoy quite passionate about Art 从口语化"很享受"升级为更精确的情感表达
a great way to relax my go-to activity for unwinding Art/Evening 从泛泛的"好方法"升级为个人化、具象的表达
I think In my opinion / In my view 通用 从口语化"我觉得"升级为更正式的观点表达
very important important / significant 通用 形容词精确化
big significant 通用 模糊量词→精确形容词
because since 通用 因果连接词正式化
but however / that said 通用 转折词升级，增加让步层次
really truly / really 通用 程度副词精确化
people individuals 通用 名词正式化
kids children 通用 口语→书面
good excellent / impressive 通用 泛用形容词→精确评价
interesting fascinating / captivating 通用 情感强度升级
a lot of many / loads of 通用 量词正式化或口语高级化
helps me relax helps me switch off / unwind 通用 动词搭配升级
I don't really connect with I don't feel a strong connection to Art 否定表达扩展，更完整
find them quite boring find them quite repetitive / slow-paced Films/Sports 模糊评价→精确特征描述
I'd rather do something I prefer activities that are more 通用 从口语省略到完整从句
good way to deal with practical way to addressing 交通 动词搭配正式化
Another good way Another practical way 交通 形容词精确化

5个关键提升动作

  1. 加具体细节：不说"I like art"，说"I'm really into painting because you can see someone's inner world through their colors"
  2. 用What强调句：不说"I was surprised that..."，说"What surprised me was that..."
  3. 加反思收尾：每段结尾加"It taught me that..."或"It made me realize that..."
  4. 用对比结构："not just X, but Y" / "while X, I don't Y"
  5. 加感官与情感词：interesting, devastating, awe-inspiring, fulfilling

详细对比案例

案例 1：Art — Yes - Passionate Do you like art?
Band 6.0
Yes, I really enjoy art—it's a great way to express emotions and ideas without using words. I especially love visiting art galleries on weekends; it helps me relax and see the world from different views. Even though I'm not good at drawing myself, I still value the creativity and effort behind every piece.
Band 7.0
Absolutely, I'm quite passionate about art because it allows people to express complex emotions and thoughts in ways that words sometimes can't. On weekends, I often visit local galleries—it's become my go-to activity for unwinding and gaining fresh views on life. Although I'm not skilled at drawing or painting myself, I deeply admire the imagination and hard work artists put into their creations.

具体升级点：

  • Yes, I really enjoy → Absolutely, I'm quite passionate about（开场词升级+情感精确化）
  • a great way → allows people to...in ways that...（从泛评到机制描述）
  • helps me relax → my go-to activity for unwinding（个人化+搭配升级）
  • not good at drawing → not skilled at drawing or painting（扩展+精确化）
  • value → deeply admire（动词强度升级）
案例 2：Sports programs — Yes Do you like watching sports programs?
Band 6.0
Yes, I really enjoy sports programs. I especially like watching live football matches because the atmosphere is so intense and exciting. They also help me keep up with my favorite teams and players. Sometimes, I even watch highlights with my friends—it's a fun way to spend time together.
Band 7.0
Absolutely, I'm quite fond of sports programs. Live football matches are my favorite—they create such an electric atmosphere that you can't help but get caught up in the excitement. I also rely on sports coverage to stay informed about my favorite teams and athletes. And on a more social note, watching match highlights with friends has become a bit of a ritual for us; it's not just about the sport, but about sharing reactions and opinions in real time.

具体升级点：

  • really enjoy → quite fond of（搭配多样化）
  • the atmosphere is so intense → create such an electric atmosphere that...（从平铺到so...that结构）
  • help me keep up → rely on...to stay informed（动词搭配升级）
  • a fun way to spend time → a bit of a ritual for us; not just about...but about...（概念升级+not only...but also变体）
  • 新增 in real time 增加细节精确度
案例 3：交通拥堵 — Public Transport How can we solve traffic jams?
Band 6.0
I think improving public transportation is the best way to reduce traffic jams. If buses and subways are easy to use, not too expensive, and always on time, more people will take them instead of driving. For example, cities like Tokyo and Singapore have very good public transport systems.
Band 7.0
In my opinion, enhancing public transportation is the most effective long-term solution to traffic congestion. When public transit is convenient, affordable, and reliable—like frequent subway services or express buses—people are far more likely to leave their cars at home. Take Tokyo or Singapore as examples: despite being densely populated, their well-well-connected and efficient public transport networks keep road traffic surprisingly manageable.

具体升级点：

  • improving → enhancing（动词正式化）
  • best way → most effective long-term solution（概念精确化）
  • easy to use, not too expensive → convenient, affordable, and reliable（三词并列升级）
  • more people will take them → people are far more likely to leave their cars at home（从正面到反面，因果更完整）
  • very good → well-well-connected and efficient（形容词精确化）
  • 新增 despite being densely populated 让步从句
案例 4：安静的地方 — University Library Describe a quiet place
Band 6.0
The quietest place I like is the top floor of my university library. It's almost completely silent there, which is perfect for studying. I've known about it since my first year. Now, I go almost every weekday to work on assignments or prepare for exams.
Band 7.0
My go-to quiet place is the top floor of my university library—it's so silent you can almost hear a pin drop. I discovered it in my first year as a student, and it quickly became my sanctuary for deep work. I head there almost every weekday to tackle assignments or study for exams, and the peaceful atmosphere always helps me stay focused, calm, and surprisingly productive.

具体升级点：

  • The quietest place I like → My go-to quiet place（个人化表达）
  • almost completely silent → so silent you can almost hear a pin drop（夸张修辞增加生动性）
  • I've known about it → I discovered it（动词精确化）
  • perfect for studying → my sanctuary for deep work（概念升华）
  • work on → tackle（动词升级）
  • 新增 and the peaceful atmosphere always helps me...focused, calm, and surprisingly productive（三词并列+感受扩展）

提升路径总结

1
第一步：替换泛用词
把 good / bad / very / really / a lot of 替换为更精确的同义词
2
第二步：增加句型种类
在回答中加入 which 从句、Although 让步、Not only...but also 等结构
3
第三步：完善因果链
在 because 后补充 If...then 条件句或 which means... 后果句
4
第四步：分层使用连接词
